news.title: Amputee World Cup 2026: Morocco and Ghana win way to final
news.lede: Morocco and Ghana will meet in the first all-African final of the Amputee World Cup on Sunday in San Juan de los Lagos, Mexico, after Morocco beat Brazil 2-1 and Ghana knocked out holders Turkey on penalties. Neither country has reached the final of the tournament before. Whatever the result, the title will go to Africa for the first time, a sign of how far the continent’s amputee football has come since Ghana finished sixth at the 2010 and 2012 editions. Morocco came from a goal down to beat Brazil 2-1 in the first semi-final on Friday, according to Hespress and Le360 Sport, which reported in Arabic and French.

news.title: Morocco vs Ghana: When and where to watch the Amputee Football World Cup final
news.lede: Morocco will face Ghana in the 2026 Amputee Football World Cup final in Mexico on Sunday, November 22, with both countries seeking their first world title in the competition. According to the official schedule published by the World Amputee Football Federation (WAFF), the final will kick off at 7:30 p.m. local time at San Martín Stadium in San Juan de los Lagos, equivalent to 2:30 a.m. Moroccan time on Monday, November 23. Supporters can watch the match live and free of charge on the federation’s official YouTube channel.

news.title: Morocco beats Guatemala 2-0 in short stature football World Cup opener
news.lede: Morocco’s national short stature football team opened its World Cup campaign with a 2-0 victory over Guatemala on Saturday evening at the Skikina indoor sports hall in Temara. The Atlas Lions secured their first three points in the opening round of the group stage, strengthening their chances of qualifying for the knockout rounds of the tournament, hosted by Morocco. The national team will face Colombia in its second group match before taking on the United States in the final round of group-stage fixtures. The opening victory puts Morocco in a favorable position ahead of its remaining matches as the team seeks to advance in the competition and challenge for the title on home soil.

news.title: Black Challenge Beat Defending Champions Turkey on Penalties to Reach 2026 Amputee World Cup Final
news.lede: Ghana’s Black Challenge have booked their place in the final of the 2026 Amputee World Cup after defeating defending champions Turkey 4-3 on penalties following a tense 1-1 draw in regulation time. The thrilling semi-final encounter saw the Ghanaian side demonstrate remarkable resilience and determination against the reigning champions, holding their nerve to secure a place in Sunday’s title decider. With neither side able to find a winner during regulation time, the contest was decided through a penalty shootout, where the Black Challenge converted four spot-kicks to overcome Turkey’s challenge. The victory represents a significant achievement for Ghana, who have now eliminated the defending champions to move within touching distance of the ultimate prize.

news.title: Serengeti Boys fight back to hold Costa Rica in World Cup opener
news.lede: Tanzania’s Under-17 national football team, the Serengeti Boys, made an impressive statement on their FIFA U-17 World Cup debut after recovering from a two-goal deficit to force a 2-2 draw against Costa Rica in their opening Group I match. Striker Faraji Kayanda emerged as Tanzania’s hero, scoring twice in the second half to rescue a valuable point for the debutants at Aspire Zone in Doha, Qatar. The result offered a strong response from head coach Elieneza Nsanganzelu’s youngsters, who looked in danger of suffering a difficult start to their maiden appearance at the global competition after conceding twice within the opening 15 minutes. Costa Rica took the lead in the eighth minute through Jefrey Urbina, who capitalised on an opportunity to put his side ahead and immediately increase the pressure on the Tanzanian youngsters.

news.title: 2026 Amputee Football World Cup: Morocco Downs Brazil 2-1 to Reach Final
news.lede: Morocco Men’s National Amputee Soccer Team continue writing history with their impressive performance at the World Cup 2026 taking place in Mexico. The Atlas Lions reached on Friday the final for the first time after beating Brazil 2-1 in a thrilling match. The Brazilians, four-time World Cup Champions, opened the score in the 37th minute but the squad of Othmane El Najmi showed a remarkable mental strength and continued playing with the same intensity. They continued attacking, competing defensively and playing with a relentless motor.
